subject: FinOptics evaluation pack, recommended models + emergency pin request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:05:00Z
Subject: Recap: FinOptics discovery — eval pack & recommended next steps

Hi team,

Quick recap from my 1:1 discovery with Ellen and Rajiv at FinOptics (they're evaluating for an extraction+classification workflow for monthly reports):

- Primary goals: reduce human review by 60% on invoice parsing and improve classification F1 on edge cases (~25% of corpus).
- Priority constraints: PII must stay in their VPC for private deployment later; initial trial can run on hosted but logs must be scrubbed.
- Baseline: currently using an in-house LLM with ~6s avg latency and intermittent hallucinations on short context.

Ask for us: they want a small eval pack to validate quality within one week (prompt-driven tests + a few hundred labeled examples). I proposed:
- Two recommended candidate families: 'redwood-gpt-medium-v1' (fast, reasonable safety) and 'redwood-llama-13b-q4' (accuracy-heavy).
- Evaluation artifacts to send: eval_prompt_sets.csv (sample prompts + expected outputs), benchmark_run_20261130.pdf (initial perf estimates), and a short harness link for automated runs.

Immediate next steps I need from you:
1) Ben — can you assemble an initial benchmark run against their sample set and call out potential regression risks? Attach any diffs and the long/short list of failure modes.
2) Marissa — prepare the customer-facing eval pack and a short runbook for executing the harness (Drive link preferred).
3) Steph/Rishi — FYI only for now; may need escalation if we see infra/regression risks.

I'll send the customer the eval pack once Ben + Marissa sign off. Target: ship to customer by 2026-12-02 EOD.

Thanks,
Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: FinOptics discovery — eval pack & recommended next steps

Thanks Neha — I'll own the packaging and customer README. Quick clarifying Qs for Ben so the eval pack is useful:

- Target metrics: is the ask strict on F1 only, or do they want precision-heavy thresholds on PII fields?
- Failure modes: please flag tokenization/normalization diffs (these bite us in extraction).

Plan: I'll produce:
- eval_prompt_sets.csv (we'll include positive/negative cases and a small 'noisy OCR' bucket)
- a README with run steps and the harness link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcEvalPack

I'll hold sending to customer until Ben's benchmark + diff report are attached.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: FinOptics discovery — eval pack & recommended next steps

Attaching initial artifacts (diff_report_1128-1122.txt, benchmark_run_20261130.pdf). High level:

- Benchmarks: redwood-llama-13b-q4 shows +6 pts F1 vs redwood-gpt-medium-v1 on their labeled set but ~2x tokens cost. Latency median: 1.4s vs 0.6s respectively.
- Observed regression risk: a runtime build we rolled on 2026-11-28 introduced a tokenizer normalization change for a small subset of unicode punctuation (affects ~3% of their corpus). The model behavior drift manifests as split tokens causing label misalignment in some invoice line items.

Recommendation (short):
1) Ship the eval pack to FinOptics as-is to capture baseline.
2) Pin customer trial to redwood-gpt-medium-v1@2026-11-22 (stable tokenizer) while we triage the tokenizer change.
3) If FinOptics prefers the higher-accuracy 13b variant, run a controlled canary with pinned kernels and monitor divergence.

Attachments: diff_report_1128-1122.txt (summary + sample failure log attached in sample_failure_log.txt).

-ben
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@finoptics.io>, Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@finoptics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:10:00Z
Subject: Eval pack incoming + temporary pin to stable model version

Hi Ellen and Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We've prepared the eval pack (attached) and are ready to hand it over. Before we run anything, an important operational note: in internal benchmarking we uncovered a tokenizer normalization change that shipped on 2026-11-28. In a small fraction of cases this causes label misalignment for tokens in your invoice parser test set.

To avoid noise in your evaluation, we propose to pin your trial to redwood-gpt-medium-v1@2026-11-22 (this is a one-click setting and does not affect your ability to later test the 13b variant). Pinning will preserve the stable tokenizer behavior while we investigate the 11/28 build.

If you approve, we'll pin immediately and run the eval harness against the pack. Next steps we propose:
- You: confirm we can pin to 11-22 (reply OK)
- Us: run the harness, share the detailed run + diff report, then schedule a 30-min follow-up to review results.

Attachments: eval_prompt_sets.csv, benchmark_run_20261130.pdf

Best,
Neha
From: Ellen Park <ellen@finoptics.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@finoptics.io>, procurement@finoptics.io
Date: 2026-12-02T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Eval pack incoming + temporary pin to stable model version

Neha —

We ran the harness against a quick subset this morning and are seeing the exact kinds of misalignment Ben called out: amounts split across tokens and wrong line-item labels. This is happening on our baseline test cases (I attached a short snippet below). This is causing us to push the pilot start out.

We need an immediate rollback to any stable state that removes this regression. Pinning is fine, but we also expect Redwood to: 1) perform a rollback on the 11/28 build to remove the regression; 2) provide a short timeline for the rollback and for remediation; and 3) let us know whether this incident will be eligible for SLA credits — procurement is cc'ed.

--- Forwarded test snippet ---
InvoiceID: 889244
Expected: "Total: $1,234.56"
Observed: "Total: $1,234 .56" (token split)

Please advise ASAP.

Ellen Park
Head of Data Science | FinOptics
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:25:00Z
Subject: URGENT: FinOptics regression — request for emergency rollback/pin and credit approval

Steph/Rishi — forwarding customer escalation (below). Key points:
- Customer saw tokenization-induced misalignment in their pilot harness; they asked for rollback + timeline + SLA credit eligibility. Procurement is involved.
- Ben recommends immediate pin to redwood-gpt-medium-v1@2026-11-22 while we triage and a rollback of the 2026-11-28 runtime build where feasible.

Proposed immediate actions (need leadership sign-off):
1) Approve one-click pin now (low risk) and notify FinOptics this morning.
2) Authorize a rollback window for the 11/28 runtime build if infra can support it (Ben, can you confirm rollback impact?).
3) Approve a provisional credit up to one month of trial usage should regression be confirmed (we can tighten once we have a post-mortem). I attached an SLA credit request form draft (sla_credit_request_form.pdf).

I'll dispatch the pin as soon as we have verbal sign-off. Customer is pushing for immediate action.

Thanks,
Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
